newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares slide after exchange rate measures.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares slide after exchange rate measures.

text.p: Chilean blue chips on Tuesday closed more than three percent lower as foreign investors responded to measures by the central bank to revalue the peso against the U.S. dollar, traders said.
Share prices should stabilize at the opening as the bolsa adjusts to the new exchange rate, they said.
"The bourse should normalise tomorrow. This is just a one-off event," one dealer said.
The selective 40-share index closed unofficially 3.38 percent lower at 111.23 points. The general index shed 1.69 percent to 5,262.13 points.
Turnover was strong at 16.9 billion pesos amid a higher-than-usual short-term speculation.

Traders said the central bank's measures effectively revalued the peso by four percent against the U.S. dollar, boosting the price of Chilean stocks for foreign buyers, who reacted by dumping local shares and Chilean-issued ADRs.
"Chilean stocks became immediately more expensive so investors ditched their ADR positions," one trader said.
On Monday, the central bank said it would change the composition of the currency basket under which the exchange rate is set and widen the peso's flotation band against the dollar.
In the long term, the move would benefit companies with dollar debts, including Endesa and fertilizer maker Soquimich, said dealers.
Declining issues included electricity stocks, with Endesa off 5.88 percent at 256 pesos, and Enersis falling 4.79 percent to 248.5 pesos.
